title: Searching Videos as Trees: Self-Correcting Agents for Grounded Long Video QA
claim: Prior agents use continuous cropping and cannot recover from early mistakes; ours navigates a discrete tree with explicit backtracking.
layout: Top example strip, two bottom panels side-by-side split by dashed divider, ✗/✓ checklists
description: The top band shows a dashed question box (a chef question, answer Pepper, clue 14:05–14:12) beside a film strip of five cooking frames and a timeline from 00:00 to 27:57 with the ground-truth interval highlighted in green. Below it, a dashed vertical line splits two panels. The left panel, titled in red 'Previous Agentic Methods with Continuous crop_video Action', shows two sequential crop_video turns that end in a wrong answer (Cheese, IoU 0) with a red X, then three red ✗ capability items. The right panel, titled in green 'Ours: VideoTreeSearch', shows a small tree of time-segment nodes with numbered arrows for zoom_in, zoom_out and a second zoom_in into another branch. It ends in the correct answer (Pepper, IoU 0.58) with a green check, then three green ✓ items. Red versus green contrast draws the eye first.
caption: Comparison between prior multi-turn cropping agents and our VideoTreeSearch (VTS) on grounded LVQA. Prior multi-turn cropping agents (bottom left) rely on a continuous crop\_video action that conflates exploration with correction. As a result, they often converge prematurely and cannot recover from early mistakes. Our proposed VideoTreeSearch (bottom right) instead organizes the video as a tree of semantically coherent segments and lets the agent navigate it through discrete actions (zoom\_in, zoom\_out, shift). This turns precise localization and backtracking from implicit capabilities into explicitly learnable behaviors.
abstract: Grounded long-video question answering (Grounded LVQA) requires answering a question about a long video while localizing the short evidence interval that supports the answer. Recent agentic methods frame this task as multi-turn exploration with a single crop_video(start, end) action, which supports coarse-to-fine narrowing but provides no primitive for fine-to-coarse backtracking. As a result, these agents typically converge prematurely and cannot recover from an early mistake. We propose VideoTreeSearch (VTS), a framework that casts grounded LVQA as iterative self-correcting search over an adaptive temporal tree. VTS constructs a non-uniform tree through adaptive temporal segmentation so that each node corresponds to a semantically coherent segment, and trains an agent to navigate the tree through four discrete operations: zoom_in, zoom_out, shift, and answer. These operations expose backtracking and recovery as explicit, learnable primitives rather than implicit behaviors. To train this navigation, we introduce a trajectory synthesis pipeline that produces multi-step paths through the tree, including deliberate detours into incorrect branches followed by recovery. We use these trajectories for supervised fine-tuning, followed by reinforcement learning with grounding and answer-accuracy rewards. On three Grounded LVQA benchmarks (CG-Bench, Haystack-LVBench, Haystack-Ego4D), VTS outperforms the strongest prior multi-turn cropping agents by +12.5 mIoU on CG-Bench and +7.4 T-F1 on Haystack-Ego4D. The learned policy also transfers to general long-video QA, surpassing all prior multi-turn cropping agents on Video-MME, MLVU, and LVBench by up to +7.1 accuracy points. Ablations confirm that self-correcting hierarchical search is the central mechanism behind these gains: removing either adaptive descent or explicit backtracking substantially degrades performance.
